quickAnswerTitle: How Nevada School Calendars Differ in 2026–27
quickAnswer: Nevada does not use one statewide student calendar. Clark County School District and Washoe County School District both start their reviewed 2026–27 calendars on August 10, but they use different break structures, calendar tracks, contingency-day rules, and ending dates. Clark County ends May 20; students following Washoe County's Balanced Calendar attend through June 4.
about:
Nevada public school calendars are published by local districts rather than as one statewide attendance schedule. That means a shared holiday name does not guarantee the same break window, staff day, contingency rule, or last day in Clark County, Washoe County, or another Nevada district.

The reviewed 2026–27 calendars show why the district source matters. Clark County School District uses a district student calendar with separate staff-development days, elementary conference rules, and contingency dates that may remain no-school days when not needed. Washoe County publishes a Balanced Calendar for most schools plus separate Gerlach, Incline, and TMCC calendars. Its June 2–4 contingency days are scheduled school days, not a reserve after the published last day.

Use the district page for first and last days, breaks, return dates, official PDFs, and one-time calendar downloads. Then check the assigned school or program for bell times, testing, athletics, graduation, and campus-specific changes.

stateSections.label: Why Nevada Contingency Days Need a District-Specific Reading
stateSections.content:
A contingency label does not describe one statewide rule. Clark County's reviewed calendar identifies November 25, March 26, and May 21 as contingency dates tied to whether they are needed. Washoe County's Balanced Calendar instead keeps June 2, 3, and 4 in the published attendance window; students are scheduled to attend, and June 4 is the last day.

Families should read the label and note on the official district calendar before treating any contingency date as a vacation or make-up day.

faqs.q: Are Nevada school calendars the same statewide?
faqs.a: No. Nevada districts publish their own calendars, so start dates, breaks, staff days, contingency rules, and last days can differ.

faqs.q: When do Nevada schools start in 2026?
faqs.a: Both reviewed 2026–27 district calendars start August 10, 2026, but that does not establish a statewide first day. Families should confirm the assigned district and calendar track.

faqs.q: When is Nevada Spring Break in 2027?
faqs.a: There is no single statewide Spring Break. Clark County's reviewed calendar lists March 15–19, while Washoe County's Balanced Calendar lists March 22–April 2.

faqs.q: Do Nevada students attend on contingency days?
faqs.a: It depends on the district and label. Washoe County's June 2–4 contingency days are scheduled days in session, while Clark County identifies separate dates that may be used if needed.

faqs.q: Which Washoe County calendar should families use?
faqs.a: Most schools use the Balanced Calendar, but Gerlach, Incline, and TMCC have separate official calendars. Families should use the track assigned to the student.

faqs.q: Can I add a Nevada school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed district pages provide an ICS file that can be imported into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. It is a one-time import, not a live district subscription.
